question: Both in Poland and throughout the EU, the bicycle has become not only a form of recreation, but also a means of everyday transport in recent years. More and more people are using bicycles to get to school, work or the shops. As the value of bicycles and the number of cyclists rise, so too does the problem of bicycle theft.

According to available data, the number of reported bicycle thefts in Poland alone exceeds 13 000 per year, which amounts to several dozen reported cases a day. The situation is also similar in other Member States. 1.
What measures is the Commission taking to combat fraud and the illegal trade in stolen bicycles?
Does the Commission plan to work towards the creation of a European register of bicycles and e-bikes in order to assist Member States in combating the cross-border trade in stolen bicycles?
